land.text: the Byelorussian SSR, which 'proclaimed the sovereignty of Belarus on 27 July 1990' and 'gained independence on 25 August 1991'

predecessors.note: The same territory under a new name: 'the country's name was changed to the Republic of Belarus on 25 August 1991' (the Belarus page; the byelorussian-soviet-socialist-republic dossier gives 19 September 1991 from another page).

correction.text: Belarus in the year of independence (25 August 1991): the same outline as Cliopatria's 1992 shape, only the years change

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria starts the Republic in 1992; the page says 'Belarus gained independence on 25 August 1991'.

1992-2023, 208,525 km2 against the infobox 207,600 km2 (ratio 1.00). In the gazetteer the shape (938 cells) lies on Natural Earth's Belarus (925 cells); its few cells in Russia, Ukraine, Poland, Lithuania and Latvia are outline noise at the border, not a claim. The page records no change of border after 1991 (treaties of 1995 and 1996 with Latvia and Lithuania 'demarcated' the borders; the Ukraine treaty of 1997 was ratified in 2009; the Lithuanian documents in February 2007).

2024, identical to the 1992 shape. The Union State with Russia is an association of two states, 'with the stated aim of deepening the relationship ... through integration in economic and defence policy', not territory; the invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 was 'staged from Belarus' territory' without any change of border.

region.text: Belarus within the former republican boundary: 'Belarus gained independence on 25 August 1991'

ledger.note: 1991, 25 August: Belarus declares independence. 'Belarus gained independence on 25 August 1991', after the parliament 'proclaimed the sovereignty of Belarus on 27 July 1990'; the Belovezha Accords of 8 December 1991 declared the Soviet Union dissolved (internationally recognised 26 December 1991). The page gives no boundary; the region is Cliopatria's 1992 shape.

certainty.note: The frontiers are the former Soviet republican boundaries; the page dates the demarcation treaties with Latvia and Lithuania to 1995 and 1996 (final Lithuanian documents February 2007) and the Ukrainian treaty of 1997 to its ratification in 2009. The Union State with Russia (restored customs controls 'along their common border in 2001') leaves the Russian frontier a state border.

sources.title: Union State
sources.note: The Community of 1996, the Union of 1997, the Union State treaty of 8 December 1999 in force on 26 January 2000; customs controls restored in 2001; staging of the 2022 invasion.

notes: Two pages opened (budget 1-2). Cliopatria's Belarus shape equals the republican border and needs no correction; the only addition is the 1991 start. The Belarus page gives 25 August 1991 as the date of both independence and the change of name to the Republic of Belarus, while the existing byelorussian-soviet-socialist-republic dossier (another batch, another page) gives 19 September 1991 for the rename; the bound is August to September 1991. The Union State of Russia and Belarus (treaties 2 April 1996, 2 April 1997, 8 December 1999, in force 26 January 2000) is an association and not territory: it needs a dossier of type umbrella, which no Cliopatria row covers (see counterparts_needing_dossiers in the report); no vassal or occupation event is recorded for it. The two pages' extracts disagree on the 2022 staging of the invasion from Belarus ('April of that year' from the Belarus page, 'February 2022' from the Union State page), so no event is dated; it is consensual and moved no border. No border event was found, so the ledger holds the birth only; no ruler list opened (the Belarus page gives Lukashenko's election in two rounds, 24 June and 10 July 1994). All regions resolve in the gazetteer.
